mainTopic: Miracle stories of poor צדיקים like רבי חנינא בן דוסא and רבי אלעזר בן פדת, and stories of Sages whose prayers brought rain.
overview: This amud is full of stories about very poor צדיקים and the power of prayer. The wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא lights an empty oven out of shame, and a miracle fills it with bread. A golden table leg is given from Heaven and then taken back, so their reward in עולם הבא stays whole. More miracles of רבי חנינא בן דוסא follow: vinegar burns all of שבת, his goats bring home bears, and a neighbor's short beams grow longer. The גמרא asks how a poor man had goats, and רב פנחס explains that they came from someone else's lost chickens. Next, the poor רבי אלעזר בן פדת dreams that he speaks with הקדוש ברוך הוא and turns down an offer to restart the world. The amud then returns to fasting for rain, with stories of רבי חמא בר חנינא, לוי (who was punished for speaking harshly to Heaven), and רבי חייא בר לוליני. It ends as רבי חייא בר לוליני begins explaining why a צדיק is compared to both a palm tree and a cedar, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The empty oven and the suspicious neighbor
steps.stepSummary: The wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא lights her oven out of embarrassment. A mean neighbor knows they have no food and comes knocking to catch her.
steps.simpleTranslation: She did this because of embarrassment. She had a mean neighbor who said: I know they have nothing at all, so what is all this smoke? She went and knocked on the door. The wife was embarrassed and went into an inner room.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: the wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא is pretending to bake, and a mean neighbor comes to expose her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife lit the oven so that nobody would see how poor they were. The neighbor knows they have nothing, so she wants to catch the lie. The wife hides in shame, which sets up the miracle in the next step.

phrases.english: because of embarrassment.
She had a certain mean neighbor,
who said: Now, I know
that they have nothing at all,
so what is all this?
She went and knocked on the door.
She was embarrassed and went into an inner room.
phrases.notes: Now the story is talking about the wife of רבי חנינא, not the neighbor.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה לַהּ הָךְ שִׁיבָבְתָא בִּישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story about the wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: the wife hides her poverty out of shame, and a neighbor comes to expose her.

steps.title: The miracle of the oven full of bread
steps.stepSummary: A miracle fills the oven with bread and the bowl with dough. The neighbor calls out that the bread is burning, and the wife calmly answers that she went in to get the shovel.
steps.simpleTranslation: A miracle happened for her: the neighbor saw the oven full of bread and the kneading bowl full of dough. She called out: So-and-so! Bring a shovel, your bread is burning! The wife answered: I went in for exactly that.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven performs a miracle so the wife of רבי חנינא בן דוסא is not embarrassed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor came to catch an empty oven, but she finds it full of real bread. The wife's answer shows she was not surprised, and the next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: A baker's shovel, used to take bread out of the oven

phrases.english: A miracle was done for her,
so that she saw the oven full of bread
and the kneading bowl full of dough.
She said to her: So-and-so, so-and-so!
Bring a shovel, because your bread is burning!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לָהּ: אַף אֲנָא לְהָכִי עֲיַילִי.
phrases.english: She said to her: I too went in for that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְעֲבִיד לַהּ נִסָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension of step 1: the hidden poverty is covered by a miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven filled the empty oven with bread to save the righteous woman from shame.

steps.title: She went in expecting the miracle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that the wife really did go in to get a shovel, because she was used to miracles.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: She really had gone in to bring a shovel, because she was used to miracles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain the wife's answer: she was not making an excuse, she truly expected the miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think she said 'I went in for the shovel' just to cover herself. The ברייתא says no, she meant it, because miracles were a normal part of life in her home.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read her answer as a cover story. The ברייתא says she honestly went to get the shovel because she trusted a miracle would happen.

phrases.english: It was taught: She too
had gone in to bring a shovel,
because she was used to miracles.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אַף הִיא לְהָבִיא מַרְדֶּה נִכְנְסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the wife meant by her answer in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife's words were sincere; she went in for the shovel because she expected a miracle.

steps.title: A prayer, and a golden table leg from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The wife asks how long they must suffer. She tells רבי חנינא בן דוסא to pray, and a hand from Heaven gives him one leg of a golden table.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife said to him: How long will we keep suffering like this? He said: What can we do? She said: Pray that they give you something. He prayed, and something like a hand came out and gave him one leg of a golden table.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins: tired of poverty, the couple ask Heaven for help, and they receive a golden table leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the miracle is wealth, not just covering up shame. The prize is strange: one leg of a golden table, which sets up the meaning revealed in the dream.

phrases.english: His wife said to him:

phrases.aramaic: עַד אֵימַת נֵיזִיל וְנִצְטַעַר כּוּלֵּי הַאי?
phrases.english: Until when will we keep on suffering so much?
He said to her: What can we do?
Pray for mercy that they give you something.
phrases.notes: The wife is the one talking here, even though the גמרא doesn't say 'she said.'

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא רַחֲמֵי, יָצְתָה כְּמִין פִּיסַּת יָד
phrases.english: He prayed, and something like the palm of a hand came out
and gave him one leg
of a golden table.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ: עַד אֵימַת נֵיזִיל וְנִצְטַעַר כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the same couple.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In answer to prayer, Heaven gave רבי חנינא בן דוסא a leg of a golden table.

steps.title: The dream of the two-legged table
steps.stepSummary: The wife dreams that in the future the צדיקים will eat at golden tables with three legs, but her husband's table will have only two.
steps.simpleTranslation: She saw in a dream: In the future the righteous will eat at a golden table with three legs, and he will eat at a table with two legs.
steps.whatsHappening: A dream shows the price of the gift: the leg they got now was taken from their reward in the World to Come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gold was not free money. It was an advance payment from their own reward in עולם הבא, so their future table would be missing a leg.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future (here, the World to Come)

phrases.english: She saw in a dream
that in the future the righteous will eat

phrases.aramaic: אַפָּתוּרָא דְּדַהֲבָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ תְּלָת כַּרְעֵי,
phrases.english: at a golden table that has three legs,
and he will eat at a table with two legs.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזְיָא בְּחֶלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the hidden cost of the gift from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking the golden leg now means a missing leg from their table in the World to Come.

steps.title: Praying to give the gift back
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן דוסא asks his wife if she is happy to have a broken table in the future. She tells him to pray for it to be taken back, and it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Are you happy that everyone will eat at a complete table and we at a table missing a leg? She said: So what can we do? Pray that they take it back from you. He prayed, and they took it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The couple decide to give back their earthly riches so their reward in the World to Come stays complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They choose lasting reward over relief from poverty now. He prays again, and the golden leg is taken away.

keyTerms.meaning: Are you content / is it okay with you

phrases.english: He said to her: Are you happy

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵיכָל אָכְלִי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אַפָּתוּרָא דְּמַשְׁלַם
phrases.english: that everyone will eat at a complete table
and we at a table that is missing a leg?
She said to him: So what can we do?
Pray for mercy that they take it back from you.
He prayed for mercy, and they took it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ: נִיחָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the dream in step 5 by giving back the gift from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They prayed for the golden leg to be taken back, and it was.

steps.title: The second miracle was greater than the first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the taking back was a bigger miracle than the giving, because Heaven normally gives and does not take back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: The last miracle was greater than the first, because we have a tradition that Heaven gives but does not take back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story with a ברייתא that judges which of the two miracles was greater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting a gift from Heaven is a miracle, but Heaven taking back a gift goes against the usual way Heaven acts. So the second miracle broke a bigger rule.

keyTerms.meaning: For we have a tradition (literally, 'we learned')

steps.whatToRemember: Heaven gives but does not take back; the return of the golden leg went against that rule, so it was the greater miracle.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a gift from Heaven is normally final, which is why giving it back took an even bigger miracle.

phrases.english: It was taught: The last miracle was greater
than the first,
for we have learned that they give
but do not take back.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: גָּדוֹל הָיָה נֵס אַחֲרוֹן יוֹתֵר מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates the two miracles from steps 4 and 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The taking back was the greater miracle, since Heaven's normal way is to give and never take back.

steps.title: The vinegar lamp on Friday night
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן דוסא's daughter lit the שבת lamp with vinegar by mistake. He tells her that the One Who makes oil burn can make vinegar burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Friday evening, רבי חנינא בן דוסא saw that his daughter was sad. He asked her why. She said she had mixed up a jar of vinegar with a jar of oil and had lit the שבת lamp with the vinegar. He told her: Why should you worry? The One Who told oil to burn can tell vinegar to burn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new miracle story about רבי חנינא בן דוסא. His daughter is upset over a mistake with the שבת lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar does not normally burn, so the daughter expects the lamp to go out and leave them in the dark. רבי חנינא בן דוסא answers that oil burning is also only because ה׳ said so. To him, the natural and the miraculous both come from the same command.

keyTerms.meaning: Evening at sunset. Here it means Friday evening, as שבת begins.
Why should you care? Why should it bother you?

steps.whyThisMatters: This story sums up רבי חנינא בן דוסא's outlook. Nature itself is ה׳'s command, so a miracle is no harder for Him than nature.

phrases.english: One Shabbat evening
phrases.notes: Literally "one evening at sunset," meaning Friday evening. We're still with רבי חנינא בן דוסא from the earlier stories.

phrases.english: he saw his daughter, that she was sad
He said to her: My daughter, why are you sad?
She said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלִי שֶׁל חוֹמֶץ נִתְחַלֵּף לִי בִּכְלִי שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן
phrases.english: I mixed up a vessel of vinegar with a vessel of oil
and I lit the Shabbat light from it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: בִּתִּי, מַאי אִכְפַּת לִךְ?
phrases.english: He said to her: My daughter, why should it bother you?
The One Who said to the oil that it should burn
He will say to the vinegar that it should burn.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד בֵּי שִׁמְשֵׁי חַזְיַיהּ לְבַרְתֵּיהּ דַּהֲווֹת עֲצִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new miracle story about the same צדיק, after the golden table story ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The One Who makes oil burn can just as easily make vinegar burn.

steps.title: The vinegar burned all of שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that the vinegar lamp burned the whole day, and they used it to light the הבדלה candle.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: The lamp kept burning the whole day, until they took fire from it for הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא finishes the vinegar story. It tells us the miracle really happened, and on a big scale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן דוסא only said the vinegar could burn. The ברייתא tells us it actually did, and for a full day, longer than an oil lamp would usually last. It even lasted long enough to light the הבדלה flame after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא taught. This brings in a ברייתא.
The blessing that ends שבת, said over a flame

phrases.english: A tanna taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה דּוֹלֵק וְהוֹלֵךְ כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
phrases.english: It kept burning the entire day
until they brought fire from it for havdala.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הָיָה דּוֹלֵק וְהוֹלֵךְ כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the result of the vinegar story from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vinegar lamp burned the whole of שבת and lit the הבדלה flame.

steps.title: The goats that brought home bears
steps.stepSummary: People complain that רבי חנינא בן דוסא's goats are doing damage. He says: if they are guilty, let bears eat them, and if not, let each one bring home a bear on its horns. That evening each goat came home with a bear on its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן דוסא had some goats. People told him the goats were causing damage. He said: If they are causing damage, let bears eat them. If not, let each one bring a bear on its horns this evening. That evening, each goat brought a bear on its horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second miracle story. This time רבי חנינא בן דוסא lets Heaven decide whether his goats are guilty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue with the people complaining. He offers a test with two possible results: bears eat the goats if they are guilty, or the goats bring back bears if they are innocent. The goats came home carrying bears, which shows they were innocent.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ הָנָךְ עִיזֵּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa had some goats
They said to him: They are causing damage.
He said: If they are causing damage
let bears eat them
and if not
let each and every one bring
this evening a bear on its horns.

phrases.aramaic: לְאוּרְתָּא אַיְיתַי כֹּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא דּוּבָּא בְּקַרְנַיְיהוּ
phrases.english: In the evening, each and every one brought a bear on its horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא הֲווֹ לֵיהּ הָנָךְ עִיזֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate miracle story about the same צדיק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven proved the goats innocent: they came home carrying bears on their horns.

steps.title: The neighbor whose beams were too short
steps.stepSummary: A neighbor's ceiling beams don't reach across her walls. רבי חנינא בן דוסא asks her name, איכו, and blesses her: 'איכו, may your beams reach.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן דוסא had a neighbor who was building a house, but the beams were too short to reach. She came to him and said: I built my house, but my beams don't reach. He asked: What is your name? She said: איכו. He said: איכו, may your beams reach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a third miracle story. A neighbor asks רבי חנינא בן דוסא for help because her building beams are too short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks her name and builds his blessing around it. Her name, איכו, sounds like a word meaning "if so," so he says, in effect, "If so, let your beams reach." The story itself doesn't say yet what happened. The next step tells us.

keyTerms.meaning: The neighbor's name. It sounds like "if so."

phrases.english: He had a certain neighbor
who was building a house
and the beams did not reach.
She came before him and said to him:
I built my house, but my beams do not reach.
He said to her: What is your name?
She said to him: Ikku.
He said: Ikku, may your beams reach.
phrases.notes: He's playing on her name: "איכו" sounds like "if so," so his blessing means "If so, may your beams reach."

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהִיא שִׁיבָבְתָא דְּקָא בָנְיָא בֵּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another separate miracle story about the same צדיק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא blessed the neighbor that her short beams should reach.

steps.title: How far the beams grew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the beams grew until they stuck out a cubit on each side. Others say pieces were added on to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: The beams grew until they stuck out a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side. Some say: they were finished with added pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא tells us what happened after the blessing. It also brings a second opinion about how the miracle worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the beams did more than just reach: they grew a full cubit past each wall. The "some say" opinion holds that the beams were extended with added pieces. The two sides disagree about how the extra length came about.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, about an arm's length
Some say. This brings in another opinion.

phrases.english: A tanna taught:
They reached until they stuck out
a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side.
And some say: they made them with added pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הִגִּיעוּ עַד שֶׁיָּצְאוּ אַמָּה לְכָאן וְאַמָּה לְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the result of the beam blessing and gives two opinions on how it happened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beams grew a cubit past each wall; another opinion says added pieces made up the extra length.

steps.title: פלימו saw the house himself
steps.stepSummary: פלימו says he saw the house with its beams sticking out a cubit on each side, and people told him that רבי חנינא בן דוסא roofed it through his prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: פלימו says: I saw that house, and its beams stuck out a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side. People told me: This is the house that רבי חנינא בן דוסא roofed through his prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with an eyewitness. פלימו saw the house, which backs up the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פלימו describes the beams sticking out a cubit on each side, just as the first opinion in the ברייתא said. The local people link the house to רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayer. So the miracle story is backed up by someone who saw the house.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayers changed nature: vinegar burned, goats brought bears, and beams grew longer. פלימו later saw the house with his own eyes.

phrases.english: It is taught: Palaimo says:
I saw that house
and its beams were sticking out
a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side
and they said to me:
This is the house that was roofed
by Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa through his prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, פְּלֵימוֹ אוֹמֵר: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אוֹתוֹ הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the beam story, and the first opinion in step 12, with an eyewitness.
steps.raayaObject: That the beams really grew to stick out a cubit on each side because of רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The eyewitness report of פלימו in a ברייתא, along with what the local people told him.

steps.title: How could a poor man own goats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the goat story: רבי חנינא בן דוסא was poor, and חכמים forbade raising small animals in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did רבי חנינא בן דוסא get goats? He was poor! And besides, חכמים said you may not raise small animals in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the goat story from step 10 and raises two problems with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Problem one: we already know רבי חנינא was very poor, so how could he afford goats? Problem two: there is a rule against raising small grazing animals in ארץ ישראל, so how could a צדיק like him keep them?

keyTerms.meaning: Small animals, like sheep and goats

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the miracle itself. The גמרא only asks how he came to own the goats at all.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa,
from where did he have goats?
phrases.notes: These are the goats from step 10 that came home with bears on their horns.

phrases.english: But he was poor!
And furthermore, the Sages said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל?
phrases.english: One may not raise small animals in Eretz Yisrael?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא מֵהֵיכָן הֲווֹ לֵיהּ עִזִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the goat story in step 10 and questions a detail of it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that רבי חנינא בן דוסא owned goats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A poor man could not afford goats, and raising small animals in ארץ ישראל is forbidden.

steps.title: The chickens left at his door
steps.stepSummary: רב פנחס explains that a man left chickens at רבי חנינא's door. רבי חנינא would not let his family eat the eggs, and when the chickens multiplied he sold them for goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פנחס said: A man once passed by רבי חנינא's door and left chickens there. רבי חנינא's wife found them. He told her: Don't eat their eggs. The eggs and chickens multiplied and bothered them, so he sold them and bought goats with the money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פנחס begins answering the question with a story about how the goats came to be in רבי חנינא's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goats were never really his. They came from lost chickens that he looked after for the owner. This explains how a poor man had goats.

keyTerms.meaning: With their money (the money from selling them)

phrases.english: Rav Pinchas said:
There was an incident: a certain man passed
by the entrance of his house
and left chickens there,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְצָאָתַן אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא,
phrases.english: and the wife of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa found them.
And he said to her: Do not eat from their eggs.
And the eggs and chickens multiplied,
and they were bothering them,
so he sold them and bought goats with their money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פִּנְחָס: מַעֲשֶׂה וְעָבַר אָדָם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 by explaining where the goats came from.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי חנינא bought and raised goats as his own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The goats came from someone else's lost chickens that he was looking after.

steps.title: The owner returns and takes the goats
steps.stepSummary: The chicken owner comes back, proves the chickens were his with an identifying sign, and receives the goats. These are the same goats that brought home the bears.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the man who lost the chickens passed by and told his friend: Here is where I left my chickens. רבי חנינא heard and asked: Do you have a sign to identify them? He said: Yes. He gave the sign and took the goats. These are the very goats that brought bears on their horns.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: the goats go back to their real owner, and the גמרא ties this to the bear miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא only held the goats for the owner and never treated them as his. This explains how a poor man came to have goats: he never bought them with his own money. The גמרא does not spell out how the second problem, the rule against raising small animals, is settled.

keyTerms.meaning: An identifying sign proving ownership of a lost object
And these are the very same ones

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן דוסא never owned the goats. He looked after a lost item for its owner and gave it all back once the owner proved it was his.

phrases.english: Once that same man passed by
who had lost the chickens,
and said to his friend:
Here is where I left my chickens.
Rabbi Ḥanina heard and said to him:
Do you have a sign to identify them?
He said to him: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לוֹ סִימָן וְנָטַל אֶת הָעִיזִּין,
phrases.english: He gave him the sign and took the goats.
And these are the very goats
that brought bears on their horns.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵן הֵן עִיזֵּי דְּאַיְיתוֹ דּוּבֵּי בְּקַרְנַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב פנחס's story and links it back to the goats from step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The goats belonged to the owner of the lost chickens. רבי חנינא only held them for him, which explains how a poor man came to have goats.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן פדת's poverty and strange sleep
steps.stepSummary: A new story: רבי אלעזר בן פדת was so poor that after bloodletting he had only garlic to eat. He fainted, and the רבנן saw him crying and laughing in his sleep, with light coming from his forehead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן פדת was very poor. He had blood let and had nothing to eat afterward, so he put a clove of garlic in his mouth. He grew weak and fell asleep. The רבנן came to visit him and saw him crying and laughing, with a ray of light shining from his forehead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about another very poor צדיק, רבי אלעזר בן פדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After bloodletting a person needs to eat, but he had nothing except garlic, and it made him faint. This scene sets up the question in the next step: why was he crying and laughing at the same time?

keyTerms.meaning: Things were tight for him (he was very poor)
A ray of fire or light

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat:
things were very tight for him.
He had "a thing" done,
phrases.notes: Literally "did a thing"; here it means he had blood let.

phrases.english: and he did not have anything to eat afterward.
He took a clove of garlic
and put it in his mouth.
His heart grew weak and he fell asleep.
The Rabbis came to check on him.
They saw him crying and laughing,
and a ray of light was coming out of his forehead.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פְּדָת דְּחִיקָא לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא טוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about another צדיק who lived in great poverty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן פדת lived in great poverty, and the רבנן saw something unusual happen to him while he slept.

steps.title: Why were you crying and laughing?
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אלעזר woke up, the רבנן asked him why he had been crying and laughing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he woke up, they asked him: Why were you crying and laughing?
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן ask about what they saw. This sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crying and laughing at the same time is strange, so the question prepares us for a dream that had both a sad part and a happy part.

phrases.english: When he woke up, they said to him:
Why were you crying and laughing?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִתְּעַר, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא קָבָכֵית וְחָיְיכַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the crying and laughing described in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי אלעזר was crying and laughing in his sleep.

steps.title: The dream: sitting with הקדוש ברוך הוא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that in his dream הקדוש ברוך הוא sat with him. He asked how long he would suffer, and ה׳ asked whether he wanted the world restarted so that he might be born at a lucky hour for a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: הקדוש ברוך הוא was sitting with me. I asked Him: Until when will I suffer in this world? He answered: אלעזר my son, do you want Me to start the world over from the beginning? Maybe you will be born at an hour of good livelihood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר begins answering the רבנן by telling them about his dream. The conversation continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳'s answer means that his poverty is tied to the hour he was born. Changing it would mean restarting the whole world, and even then it is only "maybe." This gives the reason for his crying, while the reason for his laughing still comes later.

keyTerms.meaning: I will turn it over (restart it)
An hour of livelihood (a time of birth that brings a good living)

steps.confusionAlert: ה׳ really does offer to restart the world (נִיחָא לָךְ דְּאֵפְכֵיהּ לְעָלְמָא). The point is that even such a huge change would only make a better birth hour a "maybe," not a promise.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב עִמִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, was sitting with me,
and I said to Him:
Until when will I suffer in this world?
And He said to me: Elazar, My son,
would it please you if I turned the world back to its beginning?
Perhaps you would be born at an hour of livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב עִמִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 18 by describing the dream.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a dream he spoke with הקדוש ברוך הוא about his suffering and was told it was tied to the hour of his birth. The conversation continues past this point.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks whether restarting the world is worth it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that restarting the world would only maybe help him. He asks whether more of his life is behind him or ahead of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said before Him: All this, and it is only a maybe? I asked Him: Have I lived more years already, or are more years still ahead of me?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers ה׳'s offer with two questions. He wants to know whether the offer is really worth taking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first point is that even if the whole world is restarted, a better result is not guaranteed. His second question sets up his decision: if most of his life is already over, the gain would be small.

phrases.english: I said before Him:
All this, and it's only a maybe?
I said to Him:
Is it more what I have lived
or what I will yet live?

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלֵּי הַאי, וְאֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to ה׳'s offer in step 19 to restart the world.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether more of his life has already passed or is still ahead.

steps.title: Most of his life has already passed
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ answers that the years he has already lived are more than the years he has left.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: The years you have already lived are more.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ answers רבי אלעזר's question: most of his life is already behind him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is the key fact for what comes next. A restart would only change the few years that remain.

phrases.english: He said to me: what you have lived (is more).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The years already lived are more than the years remaining.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר turns down the offer
steps.stepSummary: Since most of his life is over, רבי אלעזר says he does not want the world restarted.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said before Him: If so, I do not want it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר makes his decision and refuses the offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is simple: turning the whole world upside down, for an uncertain gain over only a few years, is not worth it.

phrases.english: I said before Him:
If so, I do not want it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לָא בָּעֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws his conclusion from ה׳'s answer in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He refuses to have the world restarted for his sake.

steps.title: The reward of thirteen rivers of balsam oil
steps.stepSummary: Because he said 'I do not want,' ה׳ promises him thirteen rivers of pure balsam oil in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: As a reward for saying 'I do not want,' I will give you in the World to Come thirteen rivers of pure balsam oil, as big as the Euphrates and the Tigris, for you to enjoy.
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ rewards רבי אלעזר for turning down the offer by promising him great pleasure in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His refusal is treated as a good act that deserves reward. The reward is huge rivers of fine oil, each as big as the great rivers of בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The Euphrates and the Tigris rivers

phrases.english: He said to me:
As a reward for this, that you said 'I do not want,'
I will give you in the World to Come
thirteen rivers of balsam oil
pure, like the Euphrates and the Tigris,
phrases.notes: Here 'like' means each river is as big as these huge rivers.

phrases.english: that you will enjoy them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהַאי אַגְרָא דַּאֲמַרְתְּ לָא בָּעֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rewards his refusal in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is promised thirteen great rivers of pure balsam oil in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Only this much?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether this is all he will get.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said before Him: This, and no more?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר boldly asks ה׳ for even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a huge reward does not stop him from asking. This sets up ה׳'s reply about the other צדיקים.

phrases.english: I said before Him:
This, and no more?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the promised reward in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether he will receive anything beyond the thirteen rivers.

steps.title: What would be left for your friends?
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ answers: if I give you more, what will I give your colleagues?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: And what will I give to your friends?
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ explains why the reward is limited: the other צדיקים need their share too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is said as if there were only so much reward to go around. This sets up רבי אלעזר's playful comeback in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to me:
And to your friends, what will I give?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for more in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: More for him would mean less for his colleagues.

steps.title: Am I asking from someone who is short?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר pushes back: ה׳ has no limits, so giving him more takes nothing away from anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to Him: Am I asking this from a person who doesn't have enough?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר challenges ה׳'s answer, saying ה׳ is not a person whose supply can run out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳'s answer assumed that reward is limited. רבי אלעזר attacks exactly that point: ה׳ has endless resources.

phrases.english: I said to Him:
And am I asking from a person who doesn't have?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲנָא מִגַּבְרָא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ בָּעֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: ה׳'s statement that more for him would leave less for others.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ה׳ has no limits, so giving one person more does not take away from anyone else.

steps.title: A loving flick on the forehead
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ playfully flicks רבי אלעזר's forehead and calls him 'my son,' and the dream ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: He flicked His finger on my forehead and said to me: Elazar, my son, I cast My arrows at you.
steps.whatsHappening: The dream ends with a warm, playful gesture from ה׳ instead of a direct answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling him 'my son' and the light touch show ה׳'s love for him. The flick on his forehead connects back to the light the רבנן saw shining there in step 17.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר chose not to have the world restarted for his own comfort. He was rewarded in עולם הבא, and ה׳ treated him with fatherly affection.

phrases.english: He struck me with a flick of the finger on my forehead,
and said to me:
Elazar, my son,
I cast My arrows at you.
phrases.notes: A playful, loving way of speaking, like a parent teasing a child.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְיַין בְּאִסְקוּטְלָא אַפּוּתַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the dream by answering the challenge in step 26 with a gesture, not words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story ends with ה׳'s affection and explains the light seen on רבי אלעזר's forehead.

steps.title: רבי חמא בר חנינא's fast brings no rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא declares a fast for rain, but no rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא declared a fast, and rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of fasting for rain and starts a new story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a problem: a great Sage fasted and was not answered. The next steps will explore why.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina declared a fast
and rain did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, returning to the theme of fasting for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast declared by רבי חמא בר חנינא did not bring rain.

steps.title: But רבי יהושע בן לוי's fast worked!
steps.stepSummary: People challenge him: when רבי יהושע בן לוי declared a fast, rain came.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But רבי יהושע בן לוי declared a fast and rain came!
steps.whatsHappening: The people compare רבי חמא to another Sage whose fast did work, and ask why his did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is a comparison: same action, different result. Something must be different.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי גָּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi declared a fast
and rain came!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי גָּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the failure described in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The failure of רבי חמא's fast.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another Sage's fast brought rain, so why not this one?

steps.title: We are not the same person
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא answers humbly: I am one person, and the son of Levi is another.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is me, and that is the son of Levi.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא explains the difference: רבי יהושע בן לוי is greater than he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He answers the comparison by pointing to the people, not the fast. Prayers are answered according to the merit of the one praying.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of Levi (רבי יהושע בן לוי)

phrases.english: He said to them:
This is me, that is the son of Levi.
phrases.notes: He means: we are different people, and he is on a higher level than me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the comparison raised in step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any fast by a great Sage should bring rain.
steps.terutzMaskana: It depends on the stature of the Sage, and רבי יהושע בן לוי is greater.

steps.title: Praying with more focus still brings no rain
steps.stepSummary: The people suggest concentrating together so the community's hearts will be humbled. They pray, but rain still does not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Let us come and focus our minds; maybe the community's hearts will break and rain will come. They prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The people try a new approach, praying with deeper focus, but it also fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They hope the community's broken hearts can make up for any lack in the Sage's merit. When this fails too, the story is set up for רבי חמא's next move.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Let us come and focus our minds,
maybe the community will break their hearts
so that rain will come.
They prayed for mercy
and rain did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּנֵיתֵי וְנִיכַוֵּין דַּעְתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי חמא's humble answer, the people suggest another way to bring rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even focused communal prayer did not bring rain.

steps.title: Do you want rain to come through us?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא asks whether they are content for rain to come on their own account.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Are you content that rain should come because of us?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא asks the people for permission before trying something bolder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He seems to want their agreement before rain comes through their own merit. This question sets up his next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it fine with you / are you content
Because of us, on our account

phrases.english: He said to them:
Is it fine with you that rain should come on our account?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיחָא לְכוּ שֶׁיָּבֹא מָטָר בִּשְׁבִילֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the prayers fail in step 31, רבי חמא proposes a new approach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the people agree that rain should come through their own merit.

steps.title: The people agree
steps.stepSummary: The people answer yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The people agree, which allows רבי חמא to go ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With their agreement, רבי חמא can now act. The next step shows what he does.

phrases.english: They said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 32.

steps.title: Sky, cover your face!
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא orders the sky to cover itself with clouds, but at first it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Sky, sky, cover your face! It did not become covered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא speaks directly to the sky and commands it to bring clouds, but nothing happens yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of only praying, he gives the sky a direct command. The first attempt fails, which sets up his rebuke in the next step.

phrases.english: He said:
Sky, sky, cover your face!
It did not become covered.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָקִיעַ רָקִיעַ כַּסֵּי פָּנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the people's agreement from step 33, רבי חמא acts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His first command to the sky does not work.

steps.title: The sky is rebuked and the rain comes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא scolds the sky for its brazen face. Then it fills with clouds and rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: How brazen is the face of the sky! It became covered, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: after רבי חמא scolds the sky, clouds gather and the rain finally comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sky had 'refused' him, so he scolded it like a disobedient person. Right after that, it obeyed and the rain came.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חמא humbly admitted he was not like רבי יהושע בן לוי. Communal prayer did not work, but once the people agreed, his direct command and rebuke to the sky brought rain.

phrases.english: He said:
How brazen is the face of the sky!
It became covered, and rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה עַזִּין פְּנֵי רָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the failed command in step 34 and finishes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After רבי חמא rebukes the sky, it fills with clouds and the rain comes.

steps.title: Levi speaks harshly to Heaven, and rain comes
steps.stepSummary: לוי declares a fast, and no rain comes. He complains to ה׳ that He sits on high without mercy. Rain comes, but לוי becomes lame.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי declared a fast, but no rain came. He said to ה׳: Master of the world! You went up and sat on high, and You do not have mercy on Your children. Rain came, and he became lame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another rain story. This time the prayer works, but the person who said it is punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי חמא, who spoke sharply to the sky, לוי spoke sharply toward ה׳ Himself. The rain came, so the prayer was answered. But he was hurt, which shows that the way he spoke was not acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the world (a way of addressing ה׳)

phrases.english: Levi decreed a fast
and rain did not come.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
You have gone up and sat on high,
and You do not have mercy on Your children.
Rain came, and he became lame.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵוִי גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא וְלָא אֲתָא מִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rain story, after the story of רבי חמא's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי's harsh prayer brought rain, but he was punished with lameness.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's lesson: never speak harshly toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from לוי's story that a person should never throw harsh words toward ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A person should never throw harsh words toward Above. A great man did that and became lame. And who was he? לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר turns the story of לוי into a general lesson for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads לוי's lameness as a punishment for his words. If even a great man like לוי was punished, everyone else should be even more careful.
steps.whatToRemember: Even when praying in real distress, a person must not speak to ה׳ with harsh accusations.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
A person should never cast
harsh words toward Above,
for a great man
cast words toward Above and became lame,
and who was he? Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לְעוֹלָם אַל יָטִיחַ אָדָם דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from לוי's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should never speak harshly toward ה׳‎; לוי was punished for it.

steps.title: But Levi became lame from bowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: was it really his words that made לוי lame? We know he became lame from showing a קידה before רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did this cause his lameness? But לוי showed a קידה in front of רבי and became lame from that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's explanation by pointing to another report about why לוי became lame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another story says לוי became lame while showing רבי a very hard kind of bow, a קידה. If so, the lameness seems to come from that injury, not from his harsh words. That would weaken רבי אלעזר's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A special, difficult kind of bowing on one's face

phrases.english: Did this cause it for him?
phrases.notes: "This" means his harsh words to ה׳.

phrases.english: But Levi demonstrated a kidda bow
before Rabbi, and became lame!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גְּרַמָא לֵיהּ? וְהָא לֵוִי אַחְוִי קִידָּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the cause given in step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that לוי's harsh words made him lame.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different source says the lameness came from showing a קידה, so the words may not have been the cause.

steps.title: Both things caused it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both the harsh words and the bowing together caused לוי's lameness.
steps.simpleTranslation: This and that both caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by joining both reports together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two stories do not contradict each other. The bowing was the way he got hurt, and his harsh words were the reason he was punished, so both played a part. רבי אלעזר's lesson still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that, both of them

phrases.english: This and that caused it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא וְהָא גְּרַמָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one thing could have caused the lameness, so the bowing rules out the words.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the words and the bowing caused it together.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר לוליני hears the clouds
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר לוליני hears clouds planning to bring rain to עמון and מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר לוליני heard these clouds saying: Let us go and pour water on עמון and מואב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new rain story. This line sets up the problem: the rain is heading to the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rain clouds exist, but they are about to go to other nations instead of to ארץ ישראל. This prepares for רבי חייא בר לוליני's prayer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: עמון and מואב, nations east of the ירדן

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Luliani
heard these clouds saying:
Let us go and pour water
on Ammon and Moab.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר לוּלְיָינִי שַׁמְעִינְהוּ לְהָנָךְ עֲנָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rain story after the story of לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The clouds were about to bring rain to עמון and מואב.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר לוליני argues the rain belongs here
steps.stepSummary: He reminds ה׳ that the nations refused the תורה, so they should not get the rain. He asks for it to fall here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to ה׳: Master of the world! When You gave the תורה to Your people ישראל, You went around to all the nations, and they did not accept it. And now You give them rain? Pour it here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר לוליני prays and makes a case for why the rain should go to ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is that the nations turned down the תורה, while ישראל accepted it. So it makes no sense for them to get the rain while ישראל goes without. Notice that, unlike לוי, he argues respectfully and does not accuse ה׳.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
When You gave the Torah to Your nation Israel,
You went around to all the nations of the world
and they did not accept it,
and now You are giving them rain?
Pour it here.
phrases.notes: He's talking to the clouds now, telling them to drop the rain in ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם! כְּשֶׁנָּתַתָּ תּוֹרָה לְעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: His response to the clouds he heard in step 40.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the nations refused the תורה, the rain should fall on ישראל.

steps.title: The clouds pour the rain in their place
steps.stepSummary: The clouds drop the rain right there, in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They poured it in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: his prayer works, and the rain falls where he asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the power of a צדיק's prayer to change where blessing goes. Unlike לוי, he is not punished, which fits רבי אלעזר's lesson about how one may speak to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: In their place, right where they were

steps.whatToRemember: A respectful argument based on ישראל's merit brought the rain, with no punishment.

phrases.english: They poured it in their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁדְיוּהּ אַדּוּכְתַּיְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of the prayer in step 41.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The prayer of רבי חייא בר לוליני brought the rain down in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Why compare the righteous to both a palm and a cedar?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר לוליני asks why the פסוק needs both comparisons, to a palm tree and to a cedar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר לוליני taught: What does the פסוק mean, "The righteous will flourish like a palm tree; he will grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon"? If it says palm, why say cedar? And if it says cedar, why say palm?
steps.whatsHappening: Since his name came up, the גמרא brings a teaching of רבי חייא בר לוליני. He opens with a question about extra words in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the צדיק to two trees. If one comparison were enough, the second would be extra. So he asks what each tree adds that the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Luliani taught:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree;
he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon"?

phrases.aramaic: אִם נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז,
phrases.english: If it states palm tree, why does it state cedar,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר?
phrases.english: and if it states cedar, why does it state palm tree?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר לוּלְיָינִי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching, brought because the same רבי was just mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the two tree comparisons adds.

steps.title: If only the palm were written
steps.stepSummary: He begins his answer: if the פסוק had said only "palm tree", we would have learned something wrong from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had said palm tree and not cedar, I would have said: just as a palm tree...
steps.whatsHappening: He starts to answer his own question. The sentence continues past this point, so this line sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His method is to show what mistake we would make with only one tree. Here he begins with the palm alone. The rest of the comparison comes in the continuation of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said, I might have thought

phrases.english: Were it stated palm tree
and were it not stated cedar,
I would say: just as a palm tree

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ נֶאֱמַר תָּמָר וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶרֶז, הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 43.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He begins explaining what we would wrongly learn if only the palm tree were mentioned.
